sections.html:
Lewisburg anchors Greenbrier County, a large mountain county in southeastern West Virginia. The 2025 population estimate is 31,578, down 4.3 percent from 32,985 at the 2020 census. Median home value is $128,900 and 72.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Nearly one housing unit in five, 19.1 percent of 17,807, stood empty in 2020, so buyers have choices and a seller should price with that in mind.

Three magisterial districts (Eastern, Western and Central) replaced ten older ones in the 1990s. The ten historic names, such as Anthony's Creek, Blue Sulphur and Meadow Bluff, still serve as tax districts, and the one for your parcel is printed on the ticket.

The assessor's office runs a calendar from July 1 through April 30.

DateWhat happens
July 1Real and personal property is assessed to the owner of record
July 15Sheriff must mail tax tickets by this date
September 1First-half taxes due for the 2.5 percent discount; farm status and business personal property filings due
October 1Personal property returns due
December 1Homestead exemption applications due
January 31Appeals to the assessor on value must be completed
FebruaryBoard of Equalization and Review hears appeals; appointments are required
March 1Second-half taxes due for the 2.5 percent discount
April 30Last day to pay without penalty

Hearings in February are by appointment only. If you want one, call the assessor in January rather than arriving unannounced.

sections.h2: How the assessor values a house
sections.html:
Every parcel is appraised as of July 1, and the assessor must see each piece of real estate in person at least once every three years, even though values are supposed to follow the market annually. The land and personal property books are due to be finished by January 30 and handed to the Board of Equalization and Review by February 1.

By March 3 the assessor certifies the assessed values to the city and town recorders, the school board, the State Board of Education and the county commission. Those bodies lay their rates from the values, and the sheriff prints tickets from the certified rates. In the office's own words, assessors determine values while the levies set by the bodies determine revenue.

The legal yardstick is 60 percent of true and actual value, meaning the price the property would bring if voluntarily offered for sale. A forced-sale price cannot be used.

Schools take about two thirds of the money. The state's 2024 tax year report shows $36,113,705 levied on all property in Greenbrier County: $23,729,173 for schools, $9,249,870 for the county, $2,955,817 for municipalities and $178,845 for the state.

By class, the real estate levy was $11,128,225 on Class II, $9,051,481 on Class III and $4,711,259 on Class IV.

Pay the Greenbrier County Sheriff's Tax Office at 912 Court Street North, Suite 3, in Lewisburg, or mail to PO Box 347, Lewisburg, WV 24901. The phone number is (304) 647-6609.

  • Online: the sheriff's site takes cards, and a 2.95 percent processor fee (minimum $2.00) is added to the tax.
  • Trouble with a card payment: the Chief Tax Deputy is at 304-647-6610.
  • Delinquent real estate taxes: pay with a cashier's check, money order, certified check or cash. Cards are not accepted for these.
  • Tax map and online filing: both are linked from the assessor's page.

State dates still apply. The first half turns delinquent October 1 and the second half April 1, and 9 percent annual interest follows.

sections.h2: What happens to a delinquent parcel?
sections.html:
The sheriff publishes a list, and a parcel can end up at a tax lien auction run through the State Auditor. A second list of land still delinquent on September 1 is prepared by September 10, and liens nobody has redeemed are certified to the Auditor on October 31.

Each listed item picks up $25 for publication and $10 per certified-mail notice. Paying the sheriff before certification takes you off the list. Afterward the owner or a lienholder can still redeem through the Auditor before the sale. A notice that never arrives does not undo a conveyance, so an outdated mailing address is a genuine risk.

Taxes for the year belong to whoever owned the property on July 1, and the deed carries a transfer tax. The recorded deed is taxed at $1.10 per $500, with a county tax of 55 cents per $500 that the commission may raise to $1.65, plus a $20 transfer fee. Sellers pay unless the buyer takes the deed without it.

A county with a farmland protection program may add a further transfer tax of up to $1.10 per $500 under a separate statute. Greenbrier has a Farmland Protection Board among its agencies, so ask the county clerk whether the extra tax applies to your sale.

Before listing, collect the payoff from the Sheriff's Tax Office, confirm the district and class with the assessor, and hand both to the title agent.

These sales can take longer because an estate or a flood history adds steps. The county lists an Estate Services office and estate forms among its agencies, which is where to start when an owner has died and a deed must eventually be signed.

A deadly flood in 2016 along the Meadow River devastated Rupert and Rainelle, and Howard Creek ran through White Sulphur Springs and the Greenbrier grounds. A seller near those waterways should expect questions about repairs. An as-is cash sale skips the repair negotiation.

Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, can claim a $20,000 reduction in assessed value, with applications due to the assessor by December 1. Farm owners file for farm valuation by September 1. The assessor's page also links to refundable income tax credits tied to timely payment of personal property taxes, and it pays to read that before the September and October filing dates.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Greenbrier County property taxes?
faqs.a: At the Sheriff's Tax Office, 912 Court Street North, Suite 3, Lewisburg, or by mail to PO Box 347, Lewisburg, WV 24901. Card payments online add a 2.95 percent fee with a $2.00 minimum.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Greenbrier County taxes without penalty?
faqs.a: April 30 is the last day without penalty on the county calendar. The second half still turns delinquent April 1 under state law, and 9 percent interest runs from that date.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Greenbrier County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. Appeals on value must be completed by January 31, and the Board of Equalization and Review hears them in February by appointment. A further appeal goes to the Office of Tax Appeals.

faqs.q: Does a Greenbrier County seller owe the tax for the whole year?
faqs.a: Whoever owns the parcel on July 1 is liable for that year's taxes. In practice the closing agent pays any open balance out of the seller's proceeds.

faqs.q: How do I get a Greenbrier County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File an application with the assessor by December 1. You must be 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, with two consecutive years of West Virginia residence.
